_note: Combination reference for /combinations. Statuses follow the TripSit taxonomy and its published community chart; wording of definitions is Bearings' own. Snapshot 2026-08-21. Unlisted pairs resolve to 'unknown' by design: silence in this file means the data is silent, not that a pairing is safe.

amphetamine.note: Alcohol masks how stimulated you are; people drink past their limit without noticing.

benzos.note: Respiratory depression — this combination is behind most downer overdoses.

caffeine.note: Caffeine masks drunkenness rather than reducing it.

ketamine.note: Nausea, staggering, and memory gaps stack harder than either alone.

lithium.note: Dehydration and electrolyte shifts affect lithium levels.

maois.note: Blood-pressure concerns mainly with older, non-selective MAOIs.

mdma.note: Confuses hydration: alcohol dehydrates while MDMA makes overheating more likely.

tramadol.note: Sedation stacks; both lower the seizure threshold.

caffeine.note: Added cardiovascular strain and jaw-clench anxiety.

cannabis.note: Heart rate adds; paranoia can too.

ketamine.note: Blood pressure and heart rate climb together.

lsd.note: Added stimulation can tip an experience into restlessness.

mdma.note: Temperature and cardiovascular load stack; most harm reports involve heavy polyuse.

cannabis.note: Heavy sedation; neither cancels the other.

ketamine.note: Blunts dissociation — clinics often withhold them for this reason.

lsd.note: The classic trip killer: reduces intensity rather than ending anything.

mdma.note: Useful for unwanted stimulation after the fact; take only if actually needed.

lsd.note: Jitter edge on top of an already-aroused nervous system.

tramadol.note: Both nudge the seizure threshold downward.

lsd.note: Late-trip amplification is the common report — fine until suddenly not.

mdma.note: Can soften the come-up or amplify anxiety; direction is unpredictable.

psilocybin.note: Same amplification story as LSD; dose the mushroom, not the joint.

maois.note: Limited data; blood pressure warrants care.

mdma.note: Common pairing; the ketamine lands differently under MDMA's threshold shift.

lithium.note: Case literature links lithium with seizures alongside classic psychedelics.

maois.note: Some potentiation reported; less characterised than psilocybin.

mdma.note: A common pairing ('flipping'). The timelines stack — plan a long day.

ssris.note: Often blunted, sometimes to nearly nothing. Do not redose to chase it.

tramadol.note: Tramadol lowers the seizure threshold across the board.

mdma.note: Case literature plus hydration and electrolyte complications — a bad overlap.

psilocybin.note: Strong potentiation — this is effectively how ayahuasca works. Dose accordingly or not at all.

ssris.note: Serotonin syndrome; switching between these medications requires a supervised washout.

psilocybin.note: 'Hippie flipping.' Which one leads shapes which experience you get.
